multipleChoice.question: What is the main benefit of scratching in the skin expert's account?
options: It identifies the exact source of an itch.
It clears potentially harmful things from the skin.
It prevents every future contact with parasites.
It makes the skin stop noticing unfamiliar objects.

multipleChoice.question: What question did the researchers set out to explore?
options: Whether itchy clothing changes how people think.
Whether parasites can be seen in a video recording.
Whether scratching removes objects from the skin faster.
Whether thinking about itching can increase itchy feelings.

multipleChoice.question: What did the video study show about its participants?
options: They felt itchier and scratched more without prompting.
They felt itchier but deliberately avoided scratching.
They scratched more only after receiving instructions.
They scratched less although they felt equally itchy.

multipleChoice.question: What does the expert's phrase "catch a scratch" suggest in this study?
options: Scratching directly transfers a skin parasite.
A person needs physical contact to begin scratching.
Seeing scratching can trigger an urge to scratch.
An itchy feeling always spreads through conversation.

multipleChoice.question: Which contrast best captures the two experts' findings?
options: One explains the cause of every itch; the other disproves that cause.
One describes a protective action; the other finds a response to what people see.
One studies skin damage; the other shows that scratching repairs damaged skin.
One rules out outside triggers; the other identifies a parasite in the videos.
